changes: The Sound checkbox is now a Music volume slider on the title screen and in the game bar. It starts at zero (silent); slide it up to hear the music.
New Sound checkbox on the title screen and in the game bar, off by default. When on, background music plays: calm tracks on the main board and faster ones during battles.
Computer players plan safer splits and movement, protect developed legions, use available reinforcements and summons, and fight more carefully around Titans and the battle clock.
Choose Easy, Normal or Hard for each computer player independently of personality. Easy uses simpler coordination between legions. Older campaigns continue on Normal.
Hard plans future recruiting routes and coordinated battle formations, simulating combat, reinforcement and summoning.
Animated mode now celebrates a new winner with their colors, a victory card and brief confetti. Reduced motion keeps the card still.
Movement-target recruit previews now compare power times skill, add one point each for flying and ranged attacks, and break ties by higher skill.
Animated main-board legion markers and muster creature icons are another 20% larger.
Animated main-board landscapes now fill their hexes with larger illustrations.
Animated main-board legion markers and muster creature icons are now 20% larger, including moving markers.
The title screen now fills the window with an illustrated fantasy landscape and clearer local and online play.
Saved campaigns have a prominent resume entry, with a roomier commander setup and a compact Appearance section.
Animated mode is now on by default, with a visible checkbox on the title screen and game toolbar. Your saved choice is kept.
Animated mode refreshes the main board with illustrated landscapes, clearer gates and labels, and new legion crests that keep player colors and full marker identities.
Animated battlefields now have illustrated terrain, stone paving, clearer elevation labels and distinct cliffs, walls, slopes, dunes and rivers.
Animated mode now zooms into the contested main-board hex as battle begins, then returns there when battle ends. Reduced motion uses a short fade.

New optional Animated presentation mode brings the 24 standard creatures to life in battles, with resting, moving and attacking artwork. Classic remains the default; reduced motion shows still artwork.
Animated mode now adds a very gentle sway or shimmer to familiar main-board landscapes, while terrain names and board pieces stay still.
Animated mode now also uses colored creature artwork for muster previews, recruited creatures, legion contents and recruit choices.
AI legions now leave room for every creature when they move onto the battle board. Before, the AI could block its own Titan from entering, so the Titan was eliminated before you had a single turn.
The game now has a version number, shown next to the Colossus title. It goes up by 0.01 with every update.
New "What's new" button: click the version number to see what changed in each version.
Already in this first numbered version: hotseat, AI and online play (GameHub), saving and loading, selectable backgrounds, and the recent fixes for the Fight! button against AI defenders.
